sources.title: ATO: Tax reform, introducing a minimum tax on discretionary trusts
sources.fact: Read 26 September 2026 (page last updated 3 September 2026). States the measure is not yet law: a 30% minimum tax on discretionary trusts from 1 July 2028 at the trustee level, with a non-refundable credit for non-corporate presently entitled beneficiaries, and a 3-year restructure rollover available from 1 July 2027. Treasury consulted on exposure draft legislation from 3 to 18 September 2026.
sources.limitations: Announced measure, not law when read. Check its current status before relying on it.

sources.title: TR 2022/4 Income tax: section 100A reimbursement agreements
sources.fact: Reviewed on 27 September 2026 at Ryan Duguid's direction: issued 8 December 2022, consolidated with an addendum 27 September 2023. States the Commissioner's view of section 100A reimbursement agreements: the connection, benefits-to-another and tax reduction purpose requirements and the ordinary dealing exception. The page states the ruling is being reviewed as a result of Commissioner of Taxation v Bendel [2026] HCA 18.
sources.limitations: Under review since the Bendel decision impact statement of 26 June 2026. Check for an addendum or withdrawal before relying on it.

sources.title: PCG 2022/2 Section 100A reimbursement agreements: ATO compliance approach
sources.fact: Reviewed on 27 September 2026 at Ryan Duguid's direction: issued 8 December 2022, updated 27 September 2023. Sets the ATO's section 100A compliance approach in white, green and red zones with worked scenarios. The page states the guideline is being reviewed as a result of Commissioner of Taxation v Bendel [2026] HCA 18.
sources.limitations: A zone describes how the ATO allocates compliance resources, not the law. Under review since 26 June 2026.

sources.title: Decision impact statement: Commissioner of Taxation v Bendel [2026] HCA 18
sources.fact: Reviewed on 27 September 2026 at Ryan Duguid's direction: published 26 June 2026 on the High Court judgment of 10 June 2026. The majority held that a private company beneficiary's unpaid entitlement, left without action, was not a loan under subsection 109D(3). The ATO will not treat such an entitlement as a Division 7A loan (paragraph 33); steps that satisfy, replace or convert it can still create a loan (paragraph 34). Subdivision EA and section 100A may still apply (paragraphs 27, 35 and 36). TD 2022/11 will be withdrawn and TR 2022/4 and PCG 2022/2 are under review (paragraphs 43 and 44).
sources.limitations: The ATO's view of the decision, not the judgment itself. Read the High Court's reasons for the facts the outcome turned on.
